original_title: Subcellular spatiotemporal proteomics delineates distinct phases of ER stress proteostatic response
title: Tracking the ER's stress response protein by protein, over time
blurb: A spatiotemporal proteomics method, SPLAT-TR, follows synthesis, degradation and localization for over 4,000 proteins through early and prolonged ER stress, splitting the proteostatic response into distinct phases instead of one averaged snapshot. More valuable as a dataset other people can mine than as a single finding.

original_title: Transfer Hydrogenation of Nitrones to Hydroxylamine Derivatives with PhSiH3
title: PhSiH3 turns nitrones into hydroxylamines, no metal required
blurb: A metal- and additive-free transfer hydrogenation that converts both ketone- and aldehyde-derived nitrones into hydroxylamines in good to excellent yield under mild conditions, scalable and tolerant of bromo, chloro, fluoro, CF3, thioether, thiophene and furan groups. Unglamorous mechanism, but one less metal to strip out of the product afterward.

original_title: Duplex Paternò–Büchi Isobaric Reagents for One-Step C═C-Resolved Lipid Isomer Quantification
title: Telling apart lipid double-bond isomers without a separate ID step
blurb: Duplex Paternò-Büchi tags (AMPE-tags) derivatize the C=C bond, pin down its exact position, and hand you relative quant, all in one reaction, for isomers that share the same mass and sum composition and would otherwise be invisible to standard lipidomics.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: (Hetero)Adamantane Synthesis: A Triple Alkylation Reaction
title: A shortcut into the adamantane cage, three alkylations at a time
blurb: A convergent triple-alkylation route assembles (hetero)adamantanes with carbon, silicon, or germanium at the bridgeheads in one go, aimed at giving surface and materials chemists an easier way into a scaffold that's normally a slog to build with interchangeable functional groups.

original_title: Chemical Design Rule for Ultraviolet-Emitting Color Centers: The Role of Host Ionicity
title: What actually sets the color of a UV color center: ionicity, not the bandgap
blurb: Zero-phonon line energy in UV single-photon emitters tracks the host's bonding character, covalent versus ionic, via the bonding-antibonding splitting of the defect states, not just how wide the bandgap is. Diamond's covalent divacancy is the test case, turning into a design rule for picking better UV-emitter hosts instead of just scanning bandgaps.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Multistate reactivity of weak-field clusters at ambient temperatures
title: Some clusters are reacting through excited states you'd never guess were populated
blurb: In polynuclear clusters, coupling between local high-spin centers can leave excited states low enough to be thermally populated at room temperature, opening reaction pathways the usual ground-state-only picture misses. Sorting out the mechanism of that is apparently the whole problem.

original_title: A 3D Cycloparaphenylene‐Cored Trimeric Electron Acceptor Regulates Acceptor Fibril Morphology for 20.6%‐Efficient Ternary Organic Solar Cells
title: A curved, 3D electron acceptor gets ternary solar cells to 20.6%
blurb: CPP-3Y bolts a cycloparaphenylene nanohoop onto Y-series acceptors, giving a radially conjugated, curved, low-crystallinity acceptor instead of the usual flat one. As a third component it reshapes acceptor fibril morphology and pushes the ternary cell to 20.6% efficiency, a rare case of 3D macrocycle topology actually paying off in device numbers.

original_title: Deoxyfluorination of Aliphatic Alcohols by PyFluor/DBU: Mechanism, Reactivity, and Substrate Selectivity
title: Why PyFluor/DBU fluorinates some alcohols and stalls on others
blurb: A mechanistic dig, theory plus experiment, into deoxyfluorination with PyFluor/DBU, mapping the competing side reactions that make certain aliphatic alcohols reluctant to fluorinate. More a substrate-selectivity explanation than a new reagent, but useful for knowing when a sluggish substrate isn't worth fighting.

original_title: Finding the Right TEMPO: Multi-Objective Virtual Screening and Experimental Validation of TEMPO Derivatives for Aqueous Redox Flow Battery Catholytes
title: Screening 182 TEMPOs to find one that won't degrade in your flow battery
blurb: A multi-objective virtual screen balancing redox potential, stability, and synthetic accessibility across 182 TEMPO derivatives for aqueous flow battery catholytes flags two unexplored candidates, MC-TEMPO and DEA-TEMPO. Redox potential and predicted degradation resistance only correlate moderately, so picking on voltage alone would miss the more stable options.

original_title: Ru Single-Atom-Nanoparticle Synergy Induces Interfacial Electron Redistribution for Complete Selectivity Reversal in CO2 Hydrogenation
title: Same Ru catalyst, two products, just by changing single atom vs. nanoparticle
blurb: Ru nanoparticles on TiO2 run the reverse water-gas shift and spit out CO, but add single Ru atoms at the nanoparticle interface and selectivity flips to about 100% methane between 250 and 400°C. In-situ spectroscopy plus DFT trace the flip to a temperature-dependent dual pathway, a full selectivity reversal from an interfacial electron effect rather than a new metal.

original_title: Rongalite-Promoted One-Pot Reductive Cyclization Strategy for the Construction of Pyrrolo[1,2-α]quinoxalines from 1-(2-Nitrophenyl)pyrroles
title: Rongalite does double duty building quinoxaline-fused pyrroles
blurb: A transition-metal-free route to pyrrolo[1,2-a]quinoxalines where rongalite both reduces the nitro group and supplies the one-carbon unit that closes the ring, all in one pot. Radical-scavenger and formaldehyde-detection control experiments back up that dual role rather than just asserting it.

original_title: Water-Steam-Assisted Synthesis of Imine-Linked COF-432 for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
title: Steam instead of solvent to grow a water-harvesting COF
blurb: COF-432, an imine-linked framework for pulling water out of air, comes out crystalline via steam-assisted synthesis instead of the usual solvent-heavy solvothermal cook. Dialing in steam source, acetic acid dosage, temperature, and time gets it there, a greener route to the same material rather than a new one.

original_title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan (DS-8201a) Versus Investigator's Choice for HER2-low Breast Cancer That Has Spread or Cannot be Surgically Removed [DESTINY-Breast04]
title: T-DXd faces off against chemo in HER2-low breast cancer
blurb: Phase 3 trial from Daiichi Sankyo pitting trastuzumab deruxtecan against the oncologist's choice of chemo, capecitabine included, in breast cancer that's metastasized or can't be resected. The HER2-low part is the interesting bit, since that's a population that historically got waved off HER2-targeted therapy entirely. Trial's completed, so results should be out there to chase down.

original_title: Sodium borohydride: repurposing from a reducing agent to a reductive cyclization reagent for N -(2-iodoaryl)acrylamides
title: NaBH4 moonlights as a cyclization reagent
blurb: Sodium borohydride, normally just the reducing agent you grab off the shelf, turns out to drive a reductive cyclization of N-(2-iodoaryl)acrylamides straight to oxindoles, no external initiator required. One less reagent cluttering the pot.

original_title: From Peripheral Ag Sites to an Ag-Based Framework: Regulating CO2 Electroreduction Selectivity and Stability in V–Ag Nanoclusters
title: Same metals, different scaffold, different CO2 chemistry
blurb: Two atomically precise V-Ag nanoclusters built from the same components come out with different architectures, one with peripheral Ag+ sites perched on a polyoxovanadate scaffold, the other with an integrated Ag-based framework. That architecture alone shifts both CO2 electroreduction selectivity and how long the catalyst holds up, a cleaner structure-property link than these nanocluster papers usually manage.

original_title: Safety Hazard of the Thermal Decomposition of Difluoromethyl and -Methoxy Arenes Catalyzed by Boron Derivatives
title: Your difluoromethoxy boronic acid might not like being warm
blurb: Prompted by actual lab incidents, a DSC study found that aryl boronic acids or boronate esters carrying a difluoromethoxy or difluoromethyl group decompose exothermically at surprisingly low temperatures, both on their own and when just sitting next to other otherwise-stable compounds. Gets worse the closer the two groups are sterically. Worth running a DSC before you scale that reaction.

original_title: CCSBase2: A Unified Benchmark Dataset and Machine Learning Framework for Robust CCS Prediction
title: A benchmark to keep CCS prediction models honest
blurb: Collision cross section is supposed to help identify unknown analytes in ion mobility-MS, but measured values are sparse and current ML predictors don't generalize well outside their training set's chemical space. CCSBase2 is a unified benchmark dataset and framework meant to actually test that generalizability instead of letting models grade their own homework.

original_title: Concise Route to a Fully Tetrazolyl-Substituted Imidazole Isomer for Connectivity-Guided Energetic Material Design
title: Same energetic imidazole, three routes, not all equal
blurb: A new fully tetrazolyl-substituted imidazole, 2,4,5-tris(1H-tetrazol-5-yl)-1H-imidazole, made concisely from a tricyanoimidazole precursor, gets lined up against two previously reported isomers with identical tetrazolyl composition. Same formula, same energetic groups, but the step count to get there differs, which is the actual finding: connectivity decides the synthesis burden, not just what atoms you end up with.

original_title: Cross-section measurement of (165)Ho(d,x) reactions and comparison of deuteron and proton activation of holmium for(165)Er production.
title: Deuterons vs protons for making Erbium-165
blurb: New cross-section measurements for holmium-165 hit with deuterons, set against proton activation, both routes eyed for producing Erbium-165. Not much more to it than the numbers, but that's exactly what isotope production planning runs on.

original_title: Multiplexed hormone immunoassays for women's health on a regenerable silicon photonic chip
title: A reusable chip that reads several hormones at once
blurb: Longitudinal hormone tracking has been stuck behind assays that are expensive, inconvenient, and can't multiplex, part of why hormone-informed care is such a neglected corner of women's health. This is the first demonstration of multiplexed hormone immunoassays on a silicon photonic chip that regenerates for reuse, aimed at routine longitudinal testing instead of one-off blood draws.

original_title: Chemodivergent Synthesis of Fused Indole and Spirocyclic Indoline Through Solo‐Coordination‐Vacant Ir(III) Pincer Complex‐Catalyzed Acylnitrenoid Transfer
title: One catalyst, one intermediate, two different indole scaffolds
blurb: A coordination-vacant Ir(III) pincer catalyst takes indole-derived dioxazolones through a shared iridium-nitrenoid intermediate, then routes it to either a fused indole or a spirocyclic indoline just by tweaking the conditions, branching via a 1,2-alkyl migration or a hydride transfer. Same starting material, same catalyst, the outcome decided after the fact.

original_title: Hydrogen Bonds Regulate Paramagnetic Spin Delocalization in Ferric Hemes
title: Hydrogen bonds as a dial for where the iron's spin goes
blurb: Using five-coordinate Fe(III) porphyrin complexes with systematically varied hydrogen bonding, this pairs experiment with theory to show H-bonds give a tunable route for spin delocalization out of the paramagnetic iron center and into the secondary coordination sphere. That kind of control has been seen in protein active sites before, but not engineered on demand in a synthetic system.

original_title: Argon Coordination to the 3d Transition-Metal Monohalides: A Systematic Study of σ-Acceptor Accessibility in Ar–MX (M = Sc–Cu; X = F, Cl, Br)
title: Argon will bond to a metal if you pick the right one
blurb: A systematic sweep of Ar coordination across the 3d monohalides, Sc through Cu with F, Cl, and Br, using DFT, EDA, and multireference calculations. The binding strength doesn't creep steadily across the row, it swings, tracking how much sigma-acceptor room is left on the metal for argon's 3p electrons to donate into. Argon is still argon, this is just finding the handful of cases where it's willing to shake hands.

original_title: Playing Domino with Carbon: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Methanol with Cobalt Phthalocyanine
title: Cobalt phthalocyanine keeps CO2 reduction going all the way to methanol
blurb: Most molecular CO2 electrocatalysts stop at CO or formate. CoPc's square-planar Co-N4 site apparently pushes through the full six-electron, six-proton chain to methanol via a cascade of proton-coupled electron transfers, one catalyst doing what usually takes a relay of them. The hard part was never getting electrons onto CO2, it's stopping hydrogen evolution and CO from winning along the way.

original_title: Ampere‐Level CO 2 ‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis Over Grain‐Boundary‐Rich Sulfur‐Doped SnO 2 in Alkaline–Neutral–Acidic Electrolytes
title: Sulfur-doped SnO2 makes formate at amp-level current, and doesn't care what electrolyte you feed it
blurb: Sn catalysts for CO2-to-formate usually lose selectivity once you push the current density up, and acidic electrolytes make it worse. Loading the SnO2 with grain boundaries and sulfur dopants reportedly keeps formate selectivity at ampere-level currents across alkaline, neutral, and acidic media alike. The acidic-media part is the one worth watching, since that's where these catalysts usually fall apart.

original_title: Linker-Dependent Conformational Switching in Side-Chain-Type Ferrocene-Functionalized Nanohoops
title: Tether length decides whether ferrocene hides inside its own nanohoop or someone else's
blurb: Two ferrocene-tethered nanohoops differing only in linker length end up with different host-guest habits: the longer tether lets ferrocene tuck into its own ring as well as a neighbor's, the medium one only does the intermolecular version. DFT puts the rotational barrier for the tethered phenyl at a mild ~23 kcal/mol, so the ferrocene can spin a full 360 degrees inward under ordinary conditions. A tidy case of a couple extra methylenes rewriting the whole binding behavior.

original_title: Direct Observation of a Hydrogen‐Bonding Assisted Quasi‐Reversible Superoxo/Peroxo Interconversion in a Heme Model
title: Watching a heme model swap between superoxo and peroxo, mid-reaction, with cyclic voltammetry
blurb: Second-sphere urea groups on an iron-porphyrin build a hydrogen-bond network around a trapped water molecule, and that network stabilizes the Fe(III)-O2 superoxo state enough to catch it interconverting with the peroxo form quasi-reversibly on ordinary CV, no exotic spectroscopy required. First direct look at that redox couple behaving this way in a heme mimic, which matters for anyone modeling how O2 actually gets handled at these metal centers.

original_title: Mechanistic insights into potassium ion promotion of formate selectivity on copper clusters during carbon dioxide electroreduction
title: Potassium ions are quietly steering copper nanoclusters toward formate
blurb: Cation effects on CO2 reduction are well known for bulk copper electrodes, but nobody had isolated what K+ specifically does at copper nanoclusters until this quantum chemical model. The ion makes CO2 adsorption more exoergic, nudging the cluster's product mix toward formate. A mechanistic result for now, from simulation rather than a working electrode.

original_title: Pinacol boronates vanishing on silica
title: Pinacol boronates vanishing on silica
blurb: Grad student here, working on borylated bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes. My substrates all carry a Bpin on a secondary sp³ carbon, and I am losing catastrophic amounts of material on every column. I've quantified it and I'd like a sanity check plus ideas. The system. Crossed [2+2] photocycloaddition of an alkenyl-Bpin diene (ITX sensitizer, 395 nm, MeCN). The reaction is clean — crude NMR/GC shows only ITX, unreacted diene and product. Conversion is typically 30–50%, so I have to separate substrate from product. 1100 mg loaded, 51% conversion, long slow column, ~400 g silica (difficult separation). Tota

original_title: Diazonium coupling
title: Diazonium coupling
blurb: https://preview.redd.it/5hhgcetecash1.png?width=873&format=png&auto=webp&s=97d21a39c2259e1dffc9e209303ea900f2858690 I'm working on the coupling of a diazonium salt to salicylic acid. I have tried several conditions using different solvents (e.g., water, EtOH, ACN) in both acidic and basic conditions. Only got a trace of the desired product (3%) when using aqueous NaOH solution as the solvent. The diazonium salt is poorly soluble in water. I wonder if anyone has experience with a similar reaction and can suggest conditions I might try. Thanks.
